prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1056; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports a wrist injury and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage is in force on the reported loss date. No coverage questions have been identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Officers confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene, and the report's description of the collision matches the initial statement.

Entry 4: Statements taken from two independent witnesses, both of whom describe the crash the same way the claimant and the other driver did. Scene photos were also reviewed and are consistent with that account.

Entry 5: Inspected the insured vehicle. Damage to the front end and airbag deployment line up well with the reported impact, and the repair estimate has been opened.

Entry 6: Reviewed the medical records. The wrist fracture is consistent with the type and force of this collision. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file will be monitored as records arrive.

Entry 7: Prior records show a minor strain in the same area many years ago, which resolved fully with no ongoing limitation. Noted for the file and for the medical reviewer.

Entry 8: At a follow-up, the claimant added some small details to the account of the accident. The core sequence of events has not changed from the original statement.

Entry 9: Photos of the vehicle show a few older scratches in areas not clearly tied to this impact. Their age is not yet established, so the appraiser has been asked to note them separately.

Entry 10: A neighbor contacted the desk and believes the vehicle was already damaged several weeks before the reported date. This is a single unverified remark and has been logged for follow-up without being treated as a finding.

Entry 11: Next steps are to request the remaining treatment records through counsel, obtain the appraiser's supplement on the older marks, and schedule a review of the neighbor's comment before any settlement discussion.
